_description: Default weights of the global layout score (one shared source read by the site and the app through _shared/ui/layout_analysis/_generated/analysis_data.js). Each weight is the number of score points one unit of the metric is worth (one percentage point, or one millimetre for distance); the sign comes from the metric's direction, so every weight is positive. « floors » gives each penalty metric (lower is better) a floor in its own unit: only the part of its value above the floor costs points (Cyanophage's optimiser), so tiny differences between good layouts do not decide the rank; 0, the default, counts the whole value. A weight of 0 (pinky_ring, added on 2026-11-19) shows a metric without moving the score until the maintainer chooses its weight. The maintainer set sfb 5 and sfb_distance 0.26 (a 1 u SFB keeps costing about 10: 5 + 0.26 × 19.05 mm; 0.5, applied first the same day, made it 14.8) and the access weights altgr_usage 5 and dead_key_usage 3 on 2026-11-19 (docs/memory/maintainer-decisions.md). « grades » are the graded costs (maintainer, 2026-11-21): each table multiplies its metric's weight by the kind of event, so one weight stays the base and the grades its scale. sfb by the rows the finger crosses (same_row, one_row, two_rows: two or more); sfs adds the skipgrams on two fingers of one hand around a key of the other hand (adjacent fingers, one_apart: a finger between them, index_pinky) to its same-finger skipgrams, which count whole; row_jump (two fingers of one hand two rows or more apart: one finger's jump is an SFB) by the same finger distance; distance by the finger that travels (pinky, ring, middle, index, thumb). Every grade at 1, the sfs ones at 0 and row_jump's weight at 0 give the single weights' score to the last bit (the flat model). The shipped grades and row_jump 2.5 (half of sfb, maintainer) are the agent's scale, proposed on 2026-11-21 from Cyanophage, genkey and Oxeylyzer and shipped after its ranking-impact report (docs/audits/layout-analysers/graded-costs-ranking.md; to review by the maintainer). The choice of each value is justified in docs/audits/layout-analysers/report.md, section « Default weights ». « change_penalty » is the optimizer's cost of leaving its start layout, in score points per % of the corpus's characters moved (each weighted by its occurrences, as layoutSimilarity weighs them): its presets, the one a page starts on, the largest weight its slider offers, and the number its « at most N changed characters » starts on (docs/design/layout-optimizer.md, « Change penalty »; decided by the agent on 2026-11-19, to review by the maintainer).
